subject: Urgent Need for Help with Nimble Code Error

messages.author: 4f5b5ca62ae4b40e
messages.subject: Urgent Need for Help with Nimble Code Error
parts:
Hello nimble community,

I am currently working on a project using Nimble and I am encountering an error that I cannot seem to resolve. Here is the context and the problem I am facing:

I have the following code:

--------
## GGUM-RANK Model

## simulation

source("utils.R")  # this file is attached

# Define dimensions for the simulation
nitems <- 15               # Number of items
npersons <- 200            # Number of persons
ntraits <- 3               # Number of traits
nitems_per_block <- 3      # Number of items per block (block size)
nblocks_per_trait <- 5     # Number of blocks per trait

nblocks <- ntraits * nblocks_per_trait / nitems_per_block
all_permutations <- admisc::permutations(1:nitems_per_block)
number_of_possiable_ranks <- nrow(all_permutations)

# traits measured by the items for each block
trait_combs <- make_trait_combs(
  ntraits, nblocks_per_trait, nitems_per_block,
  comb_blocks = "random"
)
traits_of_items <- as.numeric(t(trait_combs))

# simulate response
res_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = npersons, ncol = nblocks)

alpha <- runif(nitems, 0.75, 2.25)
tau <- runif(nitems, -1.4, -0.4)
delta <- runif(nitems, -2, 2)
theta <- sim_theta(npersons, Phi = diag(ntraits))

# the item probabilities
p_items <- matrix(NA, nrow = npersons, ncol = nitems)
for (n in 1:npersons) {
  for (i in 1:nitems) {
    num0 <- 1 + exp(alpha[i] * (3 * (theta[n, traits_of_items[i]] - delta[i])))
    num1 <- exp(alpha[i] * ((theta[n, traits_of_items[i]] - delta[i]) - tau[i])) + exp(alpha[i] * ((2 * (theta[n, traits_of_items[i]] - delta[i])) - tau[i]))
    denominator <- num0 + num1
    p_items[n, i] <- num1 / denominator
  }
}

for (n in 1:npersons) {
  prob_rank <- matrix(NA, nrow = nblocks, ncol = number_of_possiable_ranks)

  prob_vector <- p_items[n, ]
  p_blocks <- split(prob_vector, rep(1:nblocks, each = nitems_per_block))

  for (b in 1:nblocks) {
    p_items_per_block <- p_blocks[[b]]

    for (m in 1:number_of_possiable_ranks) {
      prob_rank[b, m] <- calculate_joint_probability(p_items_per_block, all_permutations[m, ])
    }
    res_mat[n, b] <- sample(1:number_of_possiable_ranks, 1, prob = prob_rank[b, ])
  }
}


## MCMC estimation

library(nimble)

# Define a function to multiply the upper triangular part of a matrix with the corresponding diagonal elements.
uppertri_mult_diag <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(mat = double(2), vec = double(1)) {
    returnType(double(2))
    p <- length(vec)
    out <- matrix(nrow = p, ncol = p, init = FALSE)
    for (i in 1:p) {
      out[, i] <- mat[, i] * vec[i]
    }
    return(out)
  }
)


mu_theta <- rep(0, ntraits)
sds <- rep(1, ntraits)

constants <- list(
  npersons = npersons,
  nitems = nitems,
  ntraits = ntraits,
  nblocks = nblocks,
  nitems_per_block = nitems_per_block,
  number_of_possiable_ranks = number_of_possiable_ranks,
  all_permutations = all_permutations,
  J_trait = traits_of_items,
  mu_theta = mu_theta, sds = sds
)

data <- list(Y = res_mat)
monitors <- c("alpha", "tau", "delta", "theta", "R")

ggum_rank <- nimbleCode({
  # Define priors for item parameters
  for (i in 1:nitems) {
    alpha[i] ~ dlnorm(0, 1)
    delta[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    tau[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
  }

  # Define the Cholesky factor of the correlation matrix for 'theta' using LKJ prior
  L_theta[1:ntraits, 1:ntraits] ~ dlkj_corr_cholesky(1, ntraits)
  R[1:ntraits, 1:ntraits] <- uppertri_mult_diag(L_theta[1:ntraits, 1:ntraits], sds[1:ntraits])

  # Define priors for 'theta', the latent traits of individuals, using multivariate normal distribution
  for (n in 1:npersons) {
    theta[n, 1:ntraits] ~ dmnorm(mu_theta[1:ntraits], cholesky = R[1:ntraits, 1:ntraits], prec_param = 0)
  }

  # Likelihood for observed data
  for (n in 1:npersons) {
    for (b in 1:nblocks) {
      Y[n, b] ~ dcat(prob[n, b, 1:number_of_possiable_ranks])
    }

    # define response probability for each individual item
    for (i in 1:nitems) {
      num0 <- 1 + exp(alpha[i] * (3 * (theta[n, J_trait[i]] - delta[i])))
      num1 <- exp(alpha[i] * ((theta[n, J_trait[i]] - delta[i]) - tau[i])) + exp(alpha[i] * ((2 * (theta[n, J_trait[i]] - delta[i])) - tau[i]))
      denominator <- num0 + num1
      p_items[n, i] <- num1 / denominator
    }

    # define the joint probability
    for (b in 1:nblocks) {
      prob_values <- p_items[n, ((b - 1) * nitems_per_block + 1):(b * nitems_per_block)]

      for (m in 1:number_of_possiable_ranks) {
       
        rank_order <- all_permutations[m, ]

        joint_prob <- 1

        for (t in 1:(nitems_per_block - 1)) {
         

          current_prob <- prob_values[rank_order[t]]
          remaining_prob <- 0

          for (tt in (t + 1):nitems_per_block) {
            remaining_prob <- remaining_prob + prob_values[rank_order[tt]]
          }

          joint_prob <- joint_prob * (current_prob / (current_prob + remaining_prob))
        }

        prob[n, b, m] <- joint_prob
      }
    }
  }
})


nimbleModel <- nimbleModel(ggum_rank, data = data, constants = constants)


# system.time(
#   fit_mod <- nimbleMCMC(
#     code = ggum_rank,
#     constants = constants, data = data,
#     inits = list(), monitors = monitors,
#     niter = 8000, nburnin = 4000, nchains = 2,
#     summary = TRUE
#   )
# )

However, when I run this code, I get the following error: "Error in genVarInfo3() : Dimension of rank_order is 0, which does not match its usage in 'current_prob <- prob_values[rank_order[t]]'."

I have carefully reviewed the code and I believe there is no obvious problem with it. I am not sure why the dimension of 'rank_order' is being considered as 0.

I would greatly appreciate any help or insights on how to resolve this issue.

Thank you in advance for your assistance.

Best regards,
Zhichen

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Urgent Need for Help with Nimble Code Error
parts:
Hi Zhichen,

In model code (but not in nimbleFunction code), one must always use indexing brackets to indicate the number of index dimensions.

So please try replacing

rank_order <- all_permutations[m, ]

with

rank_order[1:N] <- all_permutations[m, ]

(where you will have to indicate what N is or use an appropriate constant for your case.)

I hope that helps.

Perry

messages.subject: Re: Urgent Need for Help with Nimble Code Error
parts: It looks like I missed that rank_order needs to be indexed by m as well, so it needs to be an array. But then that's what all_permutations seems to be. Now that I am looking at more of your model (beyond rank_order, which I specifically searched on last time because that was involved in the error message), it appears to me that your model code re-uses nodes. That is not allowed because it is a declarative model language (not an imperative language, as most programming is, i.e. sequences of steps). Each line of code declares a relationship among model nodes, so for example once a relationship for joint_prob is declared, it can't be re-declared as some different relationship. As it happens, a question from yesterday on nimble-users was about the same topic, so I will refer you to that: https://groups.google.com/u/3/g/nimble-users/c/unfd0Jtv7VI

    p <- length(vec)
    out <- matrix(nrow = p, ncol = p, init = FALSE)
